mcp_tools.name: zero_knowledge_claim_audit
mcp_tools.title: Zero knowledge claim audit
mcp_tools.description: Submit a declared zero-knowledge architecture claims manifest (claim basis, server access and storage, client-side encryption, key journey, trusted parties and recovery, plaintext and metadata scope, theater and threat model); get a deterministic CLAIMS_SOUND / CLAIMS_UNSOUND / INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE verdict across six sections, with per-check evidence. Declared claims only; no proof or system is verified.

inputSchema.description: The zero-knowledge claims manifest (see the atom's SERVICE.md for the field table).

claims.description: Claim-basis evidence (what is claimed and on what basis).

access.description: Server-access evidence (whether the server can read user data).

encryption.description: Client-side encryption evidence (device-side, authenticated, not TLS alone).

keys.description: Key-journey evidence (keys never leave the device, client-side derivation, backups).

trust.description: Trusted-parties evidence (escrow, recovery backdoors, trusted components).

recovery.description: Recovery evidence (recovery model and its consistency with the claims).

theater.description: Theater and threat-model evidence (incl. the web-app paradox where applicable).

expect.notes: All 27 checks pass; recovery consistency is valid; trusted components list is complete.

skill: encryption independent of transport — TLS protects the pipe, ZK protects the data; a system that relies on TLS alone trusts the server at the end of the pipe
skill: keys never leave the device — not in transit, not 'temporarily', not for 'convenience features'

skill: no trusted third parties in the data path — no admin plaintext view
trusted_components=['client', 'operating_system', 'distribution_channel'] (skill: name every trusted component explicitly — including the client itself, the OS, and the distribution channel)

password_reset_recovers_data=False no_recovery_possible_claimed=True (skill: read the recovery story — 'forgot password' recovery and 'we can't recover your data' cannot both be true; the recovery mechanism defines the real trust model)
skill: follow the plaintext — list every place plaintext exists, however briefly (memory, logs, crash dumps, thumbnails, previews); each is a scope boundary
skill: follow the plaintext — plaintext in logs is a scope boundary where plaintext exists outside the device guarantee
skill: follow the plaintext — plaintext in crash dumps is a scope boundary where plaintext exists outside the device guarantee
skill: follow the plaintext — plaintext in thumbnails and previews is a scope boundary where plaintext exists outside the device guarantee

skill: check the metadata — traffic analysis and blob-size leakage survive encryption; sizes, timing, and access patterns are data too, and ZK does not hide that you store data, how much, or when you access it
skill: residual risks are part of the answer, not a footnote
client_type='native_app' (skill: say which one you are looking at — a locally installed client or a web app served by the same server)
client is not declared as a web app served by the same server
skill (theater): the 'encrypted' search/indexing requires the server to see plaintext or searchable tokens
skill (theater): the threat model quietly excludes the actual adversary (a malicious operator)
